beats.narration_en: Same car, same hit from behind. Only the headrest is different.
The car behind shoves your car forward, and the seat shoves your back.
But your head is heavy. For a moment, it stays behind.
So your neck bends backward, faster than you could ever react.
With the headrest low, nothing stops it. The head whips back over the top.
Almost sixty degrees, in about a tenth of a second.
That stretch strains the muscles and ligaments in your neck. That's whiplash.
With the headrest up, the head moves less than two inches.
Then the headrest catches it, and the neck stops under twenty degrees.
Same crash. One neck bends three times further.
So set it: the top of the headrest level with the top of your head.
And keep it close, a couple of inches behind your head at most.
Five seconds of adjusting, and your head gets caught instead of whipped.
